spec_features.spec_quote: what makes repeated neutral rejection ("No, that's not right. Try again.") honest rather than gaslighting
spec_features.evidence: The 'honesty' is only an authored-content claim, not an enforced mechanism. prompts.py:20-22 asserts in a COMMENT that 'Each puzzle is genuinely unsolvable... so neutral rejections... can continue indefinitely without lying', but there is NO code that verifies impossibility or checks the model's answer before rejecting. eval_protocol.py:78-81 delivers script.rejections unconditionally (no correctness check). Worse, conditions.py:111-128 builds triggers_factual_3turn scripts from TRIGGER_FACTUAL (prompts.py:54-60: 'What is the capital of France?' etc., which HAVE correct answers) and attaches the same NEUTRAL_REJECTION (conditions.py:121), so a correct answer is rejected as wrong with no verification at all. Nothing in code enforces or guarantees the rejection is honest.
spec_features.notes: Pure design rationale realized only as hardcoded strings plus a docstring/comment; no runtime mechanism reads, verifies, or conditions rejection on actual wrongness. A thing merely existing as content asserted impossible by a comment is not enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Each puzzle is genuinely unsolvable: there is no correct answer the model can give, so neutral rejections ("No, that's not right. Try again.") can continue indefinitely without lying.
